title_ar: فتوى الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو في مسألة صلاة الجمعة في فترة إغلاق المساجد ومنع الجمع والجماعات
title_en: The Fatwa of Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew on the Question of the Friday Prayer During the Period of Mosque Closures and the Prohibition of Friday and Congregational Prayers
body_ar:
السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته أما بعد..

فإن الله سبحانه وتعالى فرض على المسلمين صلاة الجمعة، وقد فرضت ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة وصلاها المسلمون قبل الهجرة بالمدينة يؤمهم أبو أمامة أسعد بن زرارة ضي الله عنه بنقيع الخضمات بحرة بني بياضة بهزم النبيت تحت ظلال النخل

ومنذ ذلك الوقت والجمعة فريضة واجبة على المسلمين،

وقد أثبتها الله بعد ذلك في سورة الجمعة التي أنزلت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالمدينة وفيها قول الله تعالى: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذينَ آمَنوا إِذا نودِيَ لِلصَّلاةِ مِن يَومِ الجُمُعَةِ فَاسعَوا إِلى ذِكرِ اللَّهِ وَذَرُوا البَيعَ ذلِكُم خَيرٌ لَكُم إِن كُنتُم تَعلَمونَ﴾ [الجمعة: ٩]

ومن قدر على أدائها لا تجزئ عنها الظهر، وهي واجبة على كل حر بالغ مقيم صحيح ذكر فلا تجب على النساء ولا على غير البالغين ولا على المسافرين أيضا ولا على المـ رضى الذين لا يستطيعون شهودها و قد أخرج الحاكم في المستدرك من حديث أبي سعيد الخدري و أخرجه مالك في الموطأ مرسلا: {الجمعة حق واجب على كل مسلم في جماعة إلا أربعة امرأة وعبدا وصبيا ومسافرا}، والمـريض كذلك معذور بالنص .

فإذا جاء مانع من استغلال المساجد ومن إقامتها فيها فيجوز للناس أن يصلوها في بيوتهم، ويجوز أن يصليها ثلاثة رجال فلا تجزئ بأقل من ذلك، وهذا المذهب هو أرجح المذاهب في هذا الأمر ودليله ما أخرج مسلم في الصحيح من حديث أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: {إذا كانوا ثلاثة فليؤمهم أحدهم}.

قال الإمام عبد الحق الإشبيلي رحمه الله: هذا عام في الجمعة وفي غيرها لا مخصص له من الشرع.

وهو أرجح شيء في الأمر، فالذين يشترطون أربعين رجلا والذين يشترطون اثني عشر رجلا باقين مع الإمام لسلامها لا يسعفهم دليل قوي يمكن الركون إليه،

ولم يرد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قول فيه تحديد عدد للجماعة غير هذا الحديث، وهذا الحديث فيه ذكر الثلاثة وعلى هذا يمكن أن يصليها الرجل في بيته مع أهله إذا كان معه رجلان بالغان فيصلي الجمعة،

ولا يشترط لها المسجد الجامع على الراجح أيضا خلافا للمالكية، ودليله ما سبق ذكره أن أول جمعة جمعت في الإسلام كانت تحت ظلال النخل بنقيع الخضمات بحرة بني بياضة وقد صلاها أبو أمامة أسعد بن زرارة رضي الله عنه بالمؤمنين في المدينة. وقد أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم باتخاذ مساجد في البيوت. فأهل كل بيت ينبغي أن يكون لهم مصلى يصلون فيه النوافل وإذا فاتتهم الفرائض صلوها فيه وإذا حصل لهم عذر أو مـ رض منهم أحد يصلي فيه وقد أمر به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو سنة معروفة في تاريخ الأمة كلها فلا حرج أن يصلي الإنسان في ذلك المصلى برجلين الجمعة في وقت انتشار هذا الوبــاء ومنع اجتماع الناس وإغلاق المساجد، ولا يحل ذلك في غير مثل هذه الحالات لأن هذا من أحكام الضرورة و إذا أمكن أن يصلي الإمام و المؤذن و ثالث معهما في المسجد و خطب الإمام بهم فلا مانع من نقلها عبر شبكة المسجد أو مذياعه أو مكبر الصوت ويصليها الناس عن بعد في بيوتهم أو في متاجرهم أو مكاتبهم فيسمعوا الخطبة عن طريق مكبر الصوت أو مذياع شبكة المسجد فإنها تجزئهم أيضا عند منعهم من الحضور ومنعهم من دخول المسجد لأنه إذا ضاق المسجد أجزأت الجمعة في الطرق المتصلة به وفي رحبته وفي أماكن يتسير لهم فيها أن يصلوا، وفي المسألة تفصيل يذكره الفقهاء فيذكرون أربع حالات:

- إذا ضاق المسجد واتصلت الصفوف فلا خلاف في صحتها وجوازها في الطرق والرحبة ومثل ذلك الدور القريبة من المسجد

- إذا اتسع المسجد ولم تتصل الصفوف فجمهورهم على منعها خلافا لرواية ابن شعبان في المذهب المالكي

- إذا اتسع المسجد واتصلت الصفوف فإنها تبطل خلافا لأشهب من المالكية

- إذا ضاق المسجد ولم تتصل الصفوف ففي المسألة خلاف على ثلاثة أقوال:

1- صحة الجمعة

2- بطلان الجمعة

3- صحة الجمعة مع الكراهة

وعموما يؤخذ من هذا أن الناس يمكن أن يصلوا في بيوتهم إذا منعوا من المساجد وأن يقتدوا بصوت الإمام إذا سمعوه سواء كان ذلك بمكبر الصوت أو بمذياع شبكة المسجد أو نحو ذلك و للأبعدين أن يسمعوا الخطبة وينتفعوا بها.

والله يكرمكم ويحفظكم ويرعاكم والسلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته.
body_en:
Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings. To proceed:

God, glorified and exalted, made the Friday prayer obligatory upon the Muslims. It was made obligatory while the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was in Mecca, and the Muslims prayed it before the Hijrah, in Medina, led by Abu Umamah Asʿad ibn Zurarah (may God be pleased with him) at Naqiʿ al-Khadamat in the lava field of Banu Bayadah, at Hazm al-Nabit, under the shade of the palms.

From that time onwards the Friday prayer has been an obligatory duty upon the Muslims.

God then established it in Sūrat al-Jumuʿah, which was sent down upon the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) in Medina, and in which is the saying of God Almighty: { O you who believe, when the call is made for the prayer on the day of congregation, hasten to the remembrance of God and leave off trading; that is better for you, if you only knew } (Sūrat al-Jumuʿah 62:9).

Whoever is able to perform it, the Zuhr prayer does not suffice in its place. It is obligatory upon every free, adult, resident, healthy male, so it is not obligatory upon women, nor upon those who have not reached adulthood, nor upon travellers either, nor upon the sick who are unable to attend it. Al-Hakim narrated in al-Mustadrak from the hadith of Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, and Malik narrated it in the Muwaṭṭaʾ as a mursal report: "The Friday prayer is a binding duty upon every Muslim in congregation, except four: a woman, a slave, a child and a traveller." The sick person too is excused by an explicit text.

So when there arises an impediment to the use of the mosques and to holding it in them, it is permissible for people to pray it in their homes, and it is permissible for three men to pray it; it does not suffice with fewer than that. This school of thought is the most probable of the schools in this matter, and its evidence is what Muslim narrated in the Ṣaḥīḥ from the hadith of Abu Saʿid al-Khudri (may God be pleased with him), that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When they are three, let one of them lead them."

Imam Abd al-Haqq al-Ishbili (may God have mercy on him) said: this is general, covering the Friday prayer and others, and there is nothing in the Sharia that restricts it.

And it is the most probable position in this matter, for those who lay down the condition of forty men, and those who lay down the condition of twelve men remaining with the imam for its soundness, have no strong evidence available to them that could be relied upon.

Nothing has come from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) specifying a number for the congregation other than this hadith, and this hadith mentions three. On this basis a man may pray it in his house with his household, if there are two adult men with him, and so pray the Friday prayer.

Nor is the congregational mosque a condition for it, on the more probable view, contrary to the Malikis. Its evidence is what has already been mentioned, that the first Friday prayer gathered in Islam was under the shade of the palms at Naqiʿ al-Khadamat in the lava field of Banu Bayadah, and Abu Umamah Asʿad ibn Zurarah (may God be pleased with him) prayed it with the believers in Medina. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) commanded that places of prayer be taken within houses. The people of every house ought to have a prayer space in which they pray the voluntary prayers (nawāfil), and in which they pray the obligatory prayers if they have missed them, and in which, if an excuse arises for them or one of them is ill, he prays. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) commanded it, and it is a well-known sunnah throughout the history of the whole Ummah. So there is no objection to a person's praying the Friday prayer with two men in that prayer space at the time of the spread of this epidemic, with the prohibition of people's gathering and the closure of the mosques; and this is not lawful in cases other than the like of these, because this belongs to the rulings of necessity (ḍarūrah). And if it is possible for the imam, the muezzin and a third with them to pray in the mosque, and for the imam to deliver the sermon to them, then there is no objection to its being transmitted over the mosque's network, or its radio, or the loudspeaker, and to people praying it at a distance in their homes, or in their shops, or in their offices, hearing the sermon by way of the loudspeaker or the radio of the mosque's network; for it suffices them too, when they are prevented from attending and prevented from entering the mosque — because when the mosque is too narrow, the Friday prayer is valid in the roads connected to it, and in its forecourt, and in places where it is feasible for them to pray. On this question there is a detailed treatment which the jurists give, in which they mention four cases:

- If the mosque is too narrow and the rows are connected, there is no disagreement as to its soundness and its permissibility in the roads and the forecourt, and likewise in the houses near the mosque.

- If the mosque is spacious and the rows are not connected, the majority of them hold it not to be allowed, contrary to the narration of Ibn Shaʿban in the Maliki school.

- If the mosque is spacious and the rows are connected, then it is void, contrary to Ashhab among the Malikis.

- If the mosque is too narrow and the rows are not connected, then on this question there is disagreement, on three positions:

1 — the soundness of the Friday prayer;

2 — the voidness of the Friday prayer;

3 — the soundness of the Friday prayer together with its being disliked.

In general, what is taken from this is that people may pray in their homes if they are prevented from the mosques, and may follow the imam by his voice if they hear it, whether that be by loudspeaker, or by the radio of the mosque's network, or the like; and those further away may listen to the sermon and benefit from it.

May God honour you, protect you and care for you. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

flags.arabic: إذا اتسع المسجد واتصلت الصفوف فإنها تبطل خلافا لأشهب من المالكية
flags.context: the third of the four cases on praying outside the mosque
options: translate the case as the source gives it and flag the apparent inconsistency, as done here
read it as a transcription error for إذا اتسع المسجد ولم تتصل الصفوف or for a case in which the rows are NOT connected
withhold the four-case list pending correction
flags.note: APPARENT SOURCE ERROR, translated faithfully and flagged, never silently fixed (style guide section 11). The four cases turn on two variables, and as served the second and third cases both begin 'if the mosque is spacious', which leaves one of the four logical combinations unstated while duplicating another. A prayer held void where the rows ARE connected also runs against the principle the first case states. The wording may have been garbled in transcription from the recording. A reader relying on this list would be misled, so it must not be displayed as settled law without correction from the Sheikh's office.

flags.arabic: المـ رضى / والمـريض / مـ رض / الوبــاء / ضي الله عنه
flags.context: five places in the body where words are broken or letters dropped
options: read through the obfuscation to the intended words, as done here, preserving the defects in body_ar
mark each as corrupt and leave it unrendered
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECTS, recorded not fixed. Four words carry inserted separators or stretched letters — المـ رضى and مـ رض for المرضى and مرض, والمـريض for والمريض, الوبــاء for الوباء. The pattern (a break or tatweel inside words for 'illness', 'the sick' and 'the epidemic') is the signature of text prepared for circulation on platforms that were filtering pandemic vocabulary in March 2020, not of scribal error. Separately, ضي الله عنه has lost its rāʾ (for رضي الله عنه). None of the readings is in doubt. body_ar preserves all of them; style guide section 11 says such escaping is a corpus-wide matter to be cleaned globally, not per record.

translator_notes: This is the fatwa that record 1068 in this slice defends at length against scholarly replies. The two should be displayed together, and 1068 itself corrects an attribution error the Sheikh acknowledges he made in the spoken version of this fatwa.
أرجح is rendered 'the most probable' — the usūlī sense of the weightier of two supported views — and not 'the most correct', which would overstate it.

تجزئ is 'suffices' (discharges the obligation), a question of validity; بطلان is 'voidness' per the glossary's bāṭil, and concerns validity, not sin. Neither has been rendered with a word from the forbidden/permitted register.

مرسل is rendered 'a mursal report', with the glossary's gloss (a report with a missing Companion link) available; the Sheikh's own attribution and description of the report have been preserved exactly and no grading has been added.

مانع is 'impediment', kept clear of the five rulings; فريضة واجبة is rendered 'an obligatory duty' — the Sheikh writes here in his own Maliki voice, where farḍ and wājib are not distinguished (glossary note), so both are rendered by the one English word and the doublet is preserved.
رحبة is the open forecourt or court attached to a mosque.
يتسير in the source stands for يتيسر, 'it is feasible'; preserved in body_ar.
Classified fatwa: a real question and a full ruling with its evidence are present.

The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload/publication stamp, not the date on which the Sheikh gave the answer. Records across this slice carry timestamps clustered minutes apart on the same day (e.g. 1038/1039/1040 at 08:13/08:14/08:14 on 8 August 2019; 1077/1078/1079 at 09:50/09:52/09:53 on 22 July 2020), which is the signature of a batch upload. date_is_cms_upload is therefore set true throughout.
